A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SATURN framework, models and SATURN-2.6k study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite additions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original SATURN training and evaluation results on SAT and transfer benchmarks, with curriculum ablations and reasoning analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds an SFT comparison, difficulty-metric ablation and CDCL solver measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, the difficulty estimator, curriculum transitions, GRPO objective and rewards are retained. Statements about guaranteed satisfiability and full satisfying assignments clarify the existing construction and output requirements.

E1.justification: The SAT scenarios and math, programming and GPQA coverage are retained. The new SFT baseline selects from the MATH training split within existing math coverage; the metric and CDCL analyses reuse the existing SAT benchmark.

E2.justification: v2 adds an SFT-only comparator in Table 3, four alternative difficulty-score formulations in Table 7, and a CDCL solver in Table 18. These focused additions retain the existing LLM and RL comparator sets.

E3.justification: The new SFT experiment uses 1,000 Level-5 MATH training problems for one epoch. New analyses compare difficulty-score correlations across four models and measure CDCL accuracy and runtime on 1,000 instances. Previously reported SATURN training and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds an ablation testing whether alternative sparsity and structural-complexity formulas explain model performance as well as the composite difficulty score. Existing curriculum ablations, stronger-model tests and reasoning case studies are retained.

E5.justification: New Table 7 reports means and standard deviations of R-squared values across four models. This describes cross-model dispersion, not uncertainty across training runs. No additional seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New results include the SFT baseline's 44.9 average, alternative difficulty-score correlations, and CDCL solving all 1,000 instances correctly in a reported 0.14 seconds. Existing SATURN scores are retained; the multi-stage results move from v1 Table 15 to v2 Table 5 without numerical changes.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds explicit alternative difficulty-score definitions, including a negative-log expected-solution expression and a weighted structural variant. The proposed estimator and its derivation in Equations 2 and 4–12 remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims concerning scalable SAT construction, difficulty-controlled curriculum learning, SAT performance and transfer to other reasoning tasks.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning SFT specialization and alignment tax, accuracy saturation limiting SATURN-7B's difficulty correlation, and the CDCL–LLM performance gap. Existing limitations remain. The new SFT discussion incorrectly describes Math500 as improving despite Table 3 showing 83.6 to 82.0.

D1.justification: v2 documents the SFT data selection, epoch count and template choice, and explicitly identifies the existing SAT prompt as used for training as well as evaluation. Hardware, SATURN hyperparameters and repository access remain unchanged; the specific CDCL implementation is not disclosed.

R1.justification: Four works are added on SFT versus RL, cognitive reasoning behaviors, reasoning meta-abilities and instruction following with human feedback. They support the expanded SFT and verification discussions; the main related-work positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and title edits, adds explanatory paragraphs, acknowledgements and a conference checklist, and moves multi-stage results into the main discussion. The scientific narrative and main section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the metric-comparison and CDCL tables, inserts an SFT row into Table 3, and relocates the multi-stage table. Figure assets are unchanged, although placement, captions and surrounding layout receive limited revisions.

improvement.justification: The difficulty-metric ablation and SFT/CDCL comparisons provide useful checks and context absent from v1, modestly strengthening support for the unchanged framework. The gains are limited: the SFT comparison changes both training task and learning procedure, its Math500 interpretation contradicts Table 3, and the CDCL implementation and uncertainty across training runs remain undocumented.
